::: {.callout-important}
## There is no release yet

No tag, no image on `ghcr.io`, no installable binary. Everything on this page is run from a source
checkout with pnpm, and everything on this page has actually been run — where a command belongs to
a later phase, it is marked as such and it will tell you so itself rather than half-working.

The Phase column in [the roadmap](roadmap.qmd) says when the rest arrives.
:::

## What is in the tree

Phases 1 and 2 of [the roadmap](roadmap.qmd): the library, the REST contract, the CLI, the web
client, the Zotero and Paperless-ngx migrators, the ingestion pipeline and the storage backends.

| Works now | Not yet |
|---|---|
| `recueil serve` — 124 operations over 92 paths | Published Docker image; the `deploy/` files are written but have never been run |
| `recueil import zotero` with a verification report | `recueil token`, `recueil job` — mint tokens over the API for now |
| `recueil import paperless` with a verification report | Enrichment, the checks engine, dedup (Phase 3) |
| `recueil ingest`, `recueil ingest watch` — the ten stages of CONCEPT.md §5.3 | OCR and GROBID *proved*: both adapters exist, neither has been run against the real sidecar here |
| Folder, WebDAV and IMAP sources; the YAML rule engine; the review queue | Per-page OCR — the decision is per document, so a scanned page inside a text PDF is missed |
| Local filesystem, WebDAV and S3 stores, all passing one conformance suite | The desktop shell, the mobile app, the MCP server |
| `recueil export bibtex \| biblatex \| csl-json \| ris` | translation-server integration for URL/DOI/PMID/ISBN import |
| `recueil backup` / `recueil restore` | Everything from Phase 3 on |
| `.bib` feeds for Overleaf and Quarto | |
| Web client: three-pane library, item pane, PDF reader, sources, review queue, rules editor | Annotation and saved-search UI |
| The Zotero connector endpoints answer, and are tested against verbatim upstream connector code | A capture run end to end in a browser with the extension installed |

## Build it

Node 22 or later and pnpm 9.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil.git
cd etabli-recueil
pnpm install
pnpm -r build
```

That builds every package and leaves an executable at `apps/cli/dist/index.js`. There is nothing to
install yet, so the examples below call it as `recueil` and you will want an alias:

```sh
alias recueil="$PWD/apps/cli/dist/index.js"
```

## First run

```sh
recueil serve --database ./library.db --storage ./storage
```

The database and the store are created on first start; v1 is SQLite only, so there is nothing to
install first. The resolved configuration goes to stderr, with anything credential-shaped replaced
by `****`.

```sh
curl -s http://localhost:3000/health
```

```json
{
  "status": "ok",
  "name": "recueil",
  "version": "0.0.0",
  "apiVersion": "v1",
  "mode": "server",
  "components": [
    { "name": "database", "status": "ok", "required": true, "latencyMs": 0.1 },
    { "name": "storage",  "status": "ok", "required": true },
    { "name": "search",   "status": "ok", "required": false }
  ],
  "library": { "items": 0, "documents": 0, "attachments": 0, "collections": 0 },
  "database": { "ok": true, "migrationsApplied": 4 },
  "storage": { "ok": true, "path": "/…/storage", "backend": "local" },
  "search": { "available": true, "backend": "fts5" },
  "api": { "basePath": "/api/v1", "eventSubscribers": 0, "authRequired": false }
}
```

(Timestamps elided.)

That response on an empty library was the Phase 0 exit criterion, and it is still the first thing to
check after a start.

The contract the server answers is at `/openapi.json`, and the same document is committed as
[`spec/openapi.yaml`](https://github.com/etabli-dev/etabli-recueil/blob/main/spec/openapi.yaml).
It is generated from the Zod schemas the server validates with, and a test asserts in both
directions that the document and the route table describe the same server.

### Tokens

A fresh `recueil serve` on a laptop admits a request with no credential as the single local
account, which is what makes the first five minutes usable. Set `RECUEIL_REQUIRE_AUTH=true` and
every `/api/v1` call needs a token.

`recueil token` is not implemented yet. Mint one over the API:

```sh
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/api/v1/tokens \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"laptop","scopes":["items:*","collections:*","export:read"]}'
```

The secret comes back once and is never retrievable again: the server stores its SHA-256 and
cannot reproduce it.

## Importing a Zotero library

The Zotero importer is the reason Phase 1 exists.

```sh
recueil import zotero ~/Zotero/zotero.sqlite \
  --database ./library.db \
  --storage ./storage \
  --linked-base ~/Documents/Papers \
  --report ./zotero-import
```

It reads `zotero.sqlite` — items, fields, creators, collections, tags, notes, relations, imported
and linked attachments, annotations, and citation keys from the native field, from `Extra` and from
`better-bibtex.sqlite` — hashes every attachment out of the storage directory, a linked-attachment
base directory or a directory of WebDAV zips, and writes `report.json`, `report.md` and a `_REVIEW/`
directory.

**Your Zotero library is never written to.** It is copied, opened read-only, and every statement
that is not a `SELECT` is refused; the report records the SHA-256 of the source database before and
after to prove it.

The exit code is the verdict, so a migration script cannot carry on past a failure:

| Code | Meaning |
|---:|---|
| 0 | Imported, and every check passed |
| 4 | Imported, but entries were routed to `_REVIEW/` and need a decision |
| 5 | The parity check failed — do not delete anything |

Re-running is safe. Every write is keyed by something Zotero owns, so a second run over the same
library updates the same records rather than doubling them, and `--resume` carries on from where an
interrupted run stopped.

### What the report looks like

Run against the generated fixture library in `fixtures/zotero`, which is the only library this has
been proved on so far:

```
  Zotero type        Recueil type      Zotero  Recueil  Δ
  -----------------  ----------------  ------  -------  -
  book               book                   9        9  0
  bookSection        chapter                7        7  0
  conferencePaper    conference_paper       2        2  0
  dataset            dataset                4        4  0
  journalArticle     article               21       21  0
  preprint           preprint               6        6  0
  report             report                 6        6  0
  thesis             thesis                 5        5  0
  webpage            webpage                7        7  0
  all regular items                        67       67  0

  attachments      12/14 files resolved (85.7% hash coverage), 12 distinct documents
  notes            11 · annotations 8 · collections 9 · tags 23 · creators 52
  citation keys    26 kept, 1 in conflict, 0 refused
```

Every per-type count matches `fixtures/expected-counts.json` exactly, every resolved file's SHA-256
matches the digest recorded there, and the two unresolved files are named individually with the
reason each failed — one a stored file absent from `storage/`, one a linked file recorded at an
absolute path from another machine.

**This is a fixture, not a life.** The M1 milestone asks for *your own* library imported at 100%
item count and thirty days without launching Zotero. Neither has happened. Keep Zotero installed
and read-only until your own report satisfies you.

### Other importers

```sh
recueil import bibtex refs.bib
recueil import biblatex refs.bib
recueil import ris export.ris
recueil import csl-json refs.json
```

Each has a matching exporter, because a format you can only read is a trap. EndNote XML, JabRef
groups, Mendeley and CSV are later phases.

## Importing a Paperless-ngx library

```sh
recueil import paperless \
  --url https://paperless.example \
  --token "$PAPERLESS_TOKEN" \
  --database ./library.db \
  --storage ./storage \
  --report ./paperless-import
```

It walks `/api/documents/` and the tag, correspondent, document-type, storage-path and custom-field
endpoints, downloads every original, hashes it into the content store, and writes the same shape of
report the Zotero importer does — with the same exit codes, the same idempotency and the same
`--resume`. Documents become items with the Office facet: correspondent, document date, archive
serial number, reference number, amount, due date.

Against the committed corpus in `fixtures/paperless` — 11 documents, 9 tags, 6 correspondents, 5
document types, 6 custom fields, 7 archive serial numbers — every count in the report matches
`fixtures/expected-counts.json`, and the one document whose original the server refuses to serve is
routed to the review queue with the reason rather than failing the run.

Two things to know before pointing it at a real install:

- **It speaks DRF API versions 9 and 10**, i.e. Paperless-ngx 3.x. Against a server that allows
  neither, it refuses with a named error rather than guessing at an older envelope.
- **It has never spoken to a real Paperless-ngx server.** Every wire type was transcribed from the
  published source of the release the package names, and the tests run against an in-process fake of
  it. Run it with `--dry-run` first and read the report.

## Ingesting scans, mail and shares

```sh
# One file, or a directory, straight through the pipeline
recueil ingest ~/scans/2026-03-14.pdf --source-kind scanner --rules office.yaml

# The daemon: every configured source, plus any --folder given here
recueil ingest watch --rules office.yaml
```

Sources are configured over the API — `POST /api/v1/ingestion/sources` for a watched folder, a
WebDAV collection or an IMAP mailbox — and `recueil ingest watch` polls all of them. A scanner is
not a fourth kind: an ADS-4700W writing to a share is a folder source with `sourceKind: scanner`,
and one mailing its scans is an IMAP source.

Every arrival goes through the same ten stages: hash, duplicate check, archive expansion (`.zip` and
`.eml`, recursively), type detection, OCR, metadata extraction, identifier resolution, the rule
engine, the confidence gate, and one transactional commit. A file that scores below the gate is
stored and queued for a person with the reason written down; it is never guessed at.

```sh
recueil review list          # what needs a decision, and why
recueil review accept <id>   # commit the proposal
recueil rules test office.yaml --against ~/scans   # which rules fire on what
```

Rules are YAML or JSON, editable in the web client, and a rule that sets a high confidence is what
turns a recognised scanner convention into filing with no manual step. Measured here, with a folder
source, a rule set and the daemon running: six scans dropped into a watched directory became six
searchable items in under two seconds with nothing else typed.

**OCR is off unless you turn it on.** `recueil ingest --ocr ocrmypdf` (or `RECUEIL_OCR_ENGINE` on
the server) runs the OCRmyPDF adapter against a binary on `PATH`. Without it a scan with no text
layer is stored, indexed on nothing, and queued for review — which is honest, and useless for
finding it again. The adapter has not been run against a real OCRmyPDF in this repository.

## Getting data back out

```sh
recueil export bibtex --all --out library.bib
recueil export csl-json --collection 01M0MYR90WZ4BB8YFY82QESFV7 --out chapter2.json
recueil export ris --search 'creator:müller' --out subset.ris
```

Exactly one of `--all`, `--collection`, `--search` and `--ids`. The query language is Recueil's, not
the index's: `title:`, `creator:`, `container:`, `id:`, `tag:`, `note:` and `text:`, with phrases,
prefixes, `OR`, `-exclusion` and parentheses. An unknown field name is an error rather than a
silent search for the literal string.

The document goes to stdout unless `--out` is given; the counts and the losses go to stderr, so
redirecting stdout produces a file the format can actually read. Losses are reported and never
silent — a `.bib` file cannot carry an OpenAlex id, and the export says which fields it dropped.

Citation keys are stable: a stored key is used as it stands, a pinned key is never recomputed, and
only an item with no key at all is given a generated one.

### The `.bib` endpoint

For Overleaf and Quarto, a collection is also a URL:

```
GET /api/v1/collections/{id}/bibliography.bib?token=rcu_…
```

Neither tool can set a request header, so the credential goes in the query string — and because a
token in a URL is a token in a browser history and a proxy log, a `bib_feed` token may hold read
scopes only. A write scope on one is refused when it is minted.

```sh
curl -s "http://localhost:3000/api/v1/collections/$ID/bibliography.bib?token=$TOKEN" \
  -o references.bib
```

The response is `application/x-bibtex`, carries an `ETag` and an `X-Recueil-Record-Count`, and
`?format=biblatex` switches dialect. A saved search has the same endpoint under
`/api/v1/saved-searches/{id}/bibliography.bib`.

## Backup and restore

```sh
recueil backup --out ./snapshot
cd snapshot && sha256sum -c checksums.txt      # verifiable without Recueil
recueil restore ./snapshot --into ./restored
```

A snapshot is a directory, not an archive: the database taken page by page through SQLite's online
backup API, the content-addressed store in its own layout, a `manifest.json` and a `checksums.txt`
that `sha256sum -c` can check on its own. The restore hashes every file as it copies it, and one
mismatch fails the whole thing and removes what it had written — a directory that looks like a
library and is not one is worse than no directory at all.

## The web client

```sh
pnpm --filter @recueil/web run dev
```

A keyboard-first three-pane library — collections, item list, item pane — with editing that sends
only the changed field and a PDF.js reader for the attached document, plus the Phase 2 screens: the
configured sources, the review queue, and an editor for the ingestion rule sets. It is a client of
the same REST contract as everything else; there is no privileged back channel.

`pnpm --filter @recueil/web run build` produces the static bundle in `apps/web/dist`. The server
does not serve it yet — put it behind any static host or reverse proxy and point it at the API.
